subject: Private endpoint egress assertion and proxy-fallback plan
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Allowlist / firewall requirements for our private endpoint

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We're finalizing the networking requirements for Acme Health's private deployment and need a concise egress and firewall policy to present to our security and procurement teams. High-level asks:

- Canonical list of IPs (or stable FQDNs) that the private endpoint/control plane will originate to for telemetry, license checks, updates, and metadata.
- Protocols/ports required outbound (TCP/UDP) and whether any non-443 ports are mandatory.
- Whether Redwood supports SNI-based FQDN allowlisting or if we must rely on IP ranges.
- How ephemeral/resident IP rotation is handled (we cannot accept wildly variable origin IPs without evidence).
- Operational fallback patterns (e.g., bastion/proxy) in case of transient connectivity issues; we need a runbook for auditors.

We're on a tight timeline: procurement needs a short package tonight for review. Any attachments you can provide (IP manifest, thumbprints, a short runbook) would help.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Carter
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Allowlist / firewall requirements for our private endpoint

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in David (networking), Jonas (security), and Marissa (ops) to provide the concrete artifacts. Quick summary up front:

- We will provide an "egress IP manifest" containing long-lived IPs that correspond to control-plane endpoints and telemetry collectors.
- Primary allowlist method: FQDN + SNI where possible; we can provide IP ranges as a fallback.
- Required outbound ports: TCP 443 (TLS) for control plane and telemetry; TCP 853 (DNS over TLS) is optional if you plan to TLS-inspect DNS. No other outbound ports are required for normal operation.
- Ephemeral rotation: IP rotation is limited and scheduled. We'll provide rotation windows and a signed thumbprint file for verification.
- Bastion/proxy fallback: included runbook for an ops-forwarded proxy pattern that supports NATing through a designated jump host.

Attaching the initial artifacts now (egress-ip-manifest.xlsx, controlplane-cert-thumbprint.txt, runbook-bastion-fallback.md). Please review and call out any procurement-specific formats.

Proposed next step: 30-min call today at 3pm PT to walk the package and answer quick follow-ups.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Allowlist / firewall requirements for our private endpoint

Sam / team — adding some low-level details to help your firewall/security engineers. Below are the canonical items we recommend you use directly in your allowlist policy.

1) Canonical FQDNs (SNI-first):
   - control.redwood-inference.com (TLS, client/server mTLS negotiated)
   - telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.com (TLS, outbound only)
   FQDNs are stable; SNI-aware allowlisting is supported and preferred where your firewall/proxy can filter on SNI.

2) IP fallbacks (short list excerpt; full manifest attached):
   - 198.51.100.24/32
   - 198.51.100.25/32
   - 203.0.113.8/29  (control plane NAT pool)
   Note: these CIDRs represent long-lived NAT egress addresses for the control plane. We will provide notice before rotation.

3) Ports & protocols:
   - TCP 443 (required)
   - TCP 853 (optional, if you terminate DNS over TLS to our resolver)
   - TLS version: TLS1.2+ required; we prefer TLS1.3 for telemetry.
   - mTLS: optional for additional assurance; if you enable client mTLS we will provide client certs and thumbprints (see attachment).

4) Ephemeral rotation model:
   - Rotations are scheduled (monthly for larger pools, emergency rotations as needed).
   - Each rotation pushes a signed manifest and a thumbprint file with rotation timestamp.
   - We support an overlap window (72 hours) where both old and new IPs are valid for allowlisting.

5) Bastion/proxy fallback guidance:
   - If you require strict egress IP stability, configure a customer-managed jump host (bastion) in your VPC that proxies all outbound traffic to our endpoints.
   - We recommend NAT + static IP assignment on the jump host; we document a step-by-step in the runbook.

6) Audit evidence we can provide:
   - Signed IP manifest (CSV/Excel), cert thumbprint file, and a short ops runbook.
   - Optional: we can produce a signed assertion letter for procurement on request.

If you want, we can also produce a CIDR table formatted for Cisco ASA / Palo Alto import.

— David
David Kim
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 13:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Allowlist / firewall requirements for our private endpoint

Thanks David — that level of detail is exactly what our security architects needed. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/security:

- Rotation notice: when you say "we will provide notice" — can you commit to a published calendar or at least a 7-day pre-rotation notification for planned rotations? Procurement wants SLA on notification.
- Signed assertion: please share the template for the signed assertion letter you mentioned; procurement will route for signatures.
- Evidence for SOC2 / audit: Jonas, could you call out any additional artifacts Redwood can provide that support SOC2 controls tied to egress/filtering?

We can take the runbook and manifest as-is into our review if you can confirm the rotation-notice window. If so, we'll schedule the 3pm PT call.

Regards,
Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>

Hi all — quick operational confirmations to close the loop before the call:

- Rotation notice: we will publish planned rotations to the customer portal and send e-mail notifications at least 7 days prior to a planned rotation. Emergency rotations will include as-much-notice-as-possible and a post-rotation signed manifest.
- Signed assertion: attaching a short template (we can sign and return upon procurement approval).
- SOC2 artifacts: Jonas will include a short pack with log-retention policies, access controls for the control plane, and our incident response playbook.

Call confirmed for 15:00 PT today. Agenda: review manifest, confirm IP import format for your firewall, and agree rotation-notice SLA.

Attachments: runbook-bastion-fallback.md, egress-ip-manifest.xlsx, controlplane-cert-thumbprint.txt

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
